title: Salty taste is the sensing of sodium ions
summary: A salty taste, in the OpenStax account, is the perception of sodium ions in saliva.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology says salty taste is the perception of sodium ions in saliva. Salt crystals split into sodium and chloride, the sodium concentration rises outside the taste cells, and sodium enters those cells. That entry depolarizes them. The chapter is a CC BY explanation of this one taste, not a nutrition rule.

sources.title: 14.1 Sensory Perception
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, section 14.1, CC BY 4.0. No revision date was printed on the page. Supports salty taste as perception of sodium ions entering gustatory cells.
